hero.title: GIF tools that never see your file
hero.lead: Drop a GIF and pick what to do with it. The work happens in this tab, on your machine — nothing is uploaded, and there is no account to make first.
hero.dropzoneTitle: Drop a GIF here or click to browse
hero.dropzoneCaption: or paste with Ctrl+V · .gif · your file is read where it sits and goes no further
hero.reassurance: We read the first few kilobytes to work out what your file actually is. That happens here, in the page, and it is the only thing that happens before you choose a tool.

picker.heading: What would you like to do with it?
picker.unsupportedTitle: We know what this is. We can't work on it yet.
picker.unsupportedBody: Every tool here takes GIFs today. Yours isn't one, so there is nothing honest to point you at — more formats are being built.

grid.heading: Every tool, in your browser
grid.subhead: These are the ones that are finished. More are being built, and none of them will ask you to upload anything either.

why.heading: The work happens in this tab
why.body: Your GIF is decoded, changed and re-encoded by code running in your browser, on your processor. There is no queue, no upload bar, and nothing to wait behind. Close the tab mid-job and the job is simply gone — there is nowhere else for it to be.

why.heading: There is no server to trust
why.body: This is not a promise about how we handle your files. It is a statement about the shape of the thing: no free operation on this site sends bytes anywhere, because nothing on the other end is listening for them. The privacy policy is short for the same reason.

why.heading: It uses gifski, and it says how long it took
why.body: gifski builds a palette for every frame instead of one palette for the whole animation. A single palette has to average a gradient across the entire clip; a per-frame one only has to describe the frame in front of it. Every job shows you its real byte count and its real duration when it finishes.
why.evidence: A 48-frame 320×180 GIF encoded in 0.69 s — measured in Chrome on an 8-core, 16 GB laptop. Yours will differ.

discord.heading: Going to Discord?
discord.body: Discord rejects a file for reasons it does not explain, and the usual fix is to guess at a size and try again. Presets that aim straight at the limit are the next thing being built.

meta.title: PZGIF — GIF tools that run in your browser
meta.description: Compress, resize, crop, speed up and reverse GIFs without uploading them. Everything runs inside your own browser tab. No account, no server copy.
